column4: We clean and replace LI840A components as necessary and do not send units in for service unless absolutely required. Calibration functions were generated using 4 gas standard cylinders with nominal concentrations of 150, 450, 750, 1550 ppm. Calibration function offsets are tracked and used as a metric of drift. When the calibration function offset exceeds 30, the unit would be cleaned, re-zeroed, and re-spanned using CO2-free air and the high CO2 gas standard (nominally 1500 ppm). Gas standards are provideb by Linde, and were re-calibrated using a zero (N2) and standard gas cylinder from NOAA ESRL that was traceable to WMO (1567.44 ppm).

Sea-Bird Electronics SBE 45 MicroTSG Thermosalinograph; Honeywell ASCX Microstructure Pressure Sensor with 2 hPa uncertainty and an Omega Fast Response Resistance Temperature Detector with an estimated 0.164 degrees C.

column4: SBE 45 was cleaned periodically during deployment and replaced with a newly serviced unit each 12 months

Equilibrator T from the RTD closely matched T from the SBE 45 (slope = 1.006, offset = 0.129; RMSE =  0.164). However the RTD was at times noisy and intermittent. Therefor we consider equilibrator T to equal the SBE 45 T, but have combined the uncertainty in the RTD T (RMSE) with the uncertainty in the TSG T (added in quadrature) to estimate the total uncertainty of equilibrator T. The total uncertainty of equilibrator T is  estimated to be 0.164 degrees C. Intake temperature sensors were also deployed in subsequent periods of this dataset, and the average difference between the intake temperature records and the TSG T was used to correct fCO2@equil_T to fCO2@SST. The average difference was 0.14 degrees C with an uncertainty (1 standard deviation) of 0.18 degrees C.

Evans, W., Pocock, K., Hare, A., Weekes, C., Hales, B., Jackson, J., Gurney-Smith, H., Mathis, J.T., Alin, S.R., and Feely, R.A. (2019). Marine CO2 Patterns in the Northern Salish Sea. Frontiers in Marine Science 5, doi: 10.3389/fmars.2018.00536.

We estimate the total uncertainty in our determinations of fCO2@SST (pCO2@SST) to equal 1% with the following uncertainties added in quadrature: LI840A uncertainty (1 ppm), calibration uncertainty (0.5 ppm), equilibrator temperature uncertainty (0.164 degrees C), equilibrator pressure uncertainty (2 hPa), and uncertainty in the warming correction (0.18 degrees C).
